findings.title: Persistent keyspace USE failure causes endless refill loop, pool goes Broken
findings.claim: Only use_keyspace() writes current_keyspace, before any USE succeeds, and the new failure branch never clears it, so every refill resends the same failing USE forever when a keyspace is dropped, has revoked permissions, or never existed. As connections break, the pool drains and reports Broken(UseKeyspaceError), yet refilling continues endlessly opening and dropping a connection each cycle until a valid keyspace is set. Base instead logged a warning and admitted the connection so fully-qualified queries kept working, and the new branch doesn't distinguish a transient BrokenConnectionError from a nonexistent keyspace.

findings.title: Repeated keyspace USE failures are silent at default log verbosity
findings.claim: Base logged repeated keyspace USE failures with warn!, but head downgrades this to debug!, and Broken is only published when the pool is not filling and empty. So while the pool is partly full, a failure occurring on every refill cycle stays silent at default log levels.

findings.title: A hung USE delays the new failure reporting indefinitely
findings.claim: A USE that never answers keeps its future sitting in ready_connections, which keeps is_filling() true indefinitely because of a pre-existing missing timeout. As a result the new Broken report never fires and no refill gets scheduled, so the new failure-reporting branch depends on that hung future ever completing.

findings.title: Test injects a UseKeyspaceError variant the per-connection USE path can't produce
findings.claim: The test keyspace_setup_failure_triggers_refill injects UseKeyspaceError::RequestTimeout, but the per-connection USE path cannot actually produce that variant—only the pool-wide use_keyspace() call can. So the test stimulus does not match what production code can generate.

findings.title: Test coverage is weaker than the test names suggest
findings.claim: triggers_refill only asserts need_filling() and never calls run() to show a refill actually happens, so the test name overstates what's verified. Untested scenarios include a failure while other connection attempts are in flight, a persistent failure as existing connections expire, a hung USE, and a keyspace change while a USE is in flight, which discards a connection that could have been re-USEd because the keyspace_name check at line 915 only runs on the Ok path. The metrics assertions are also gated behind #[cfg(feature = "metrics")] without the validation command showing that feature enabled.

findings.title: Stale comment describes old behavior for failed USE connections
findings.claim: The comment says a failed connection 'will travel through this logic again, to be finally put into the conns,' but after this PR a failed USE instead discards the connection, making the comment stale.

findings.title: Test cleanup relies on runtime teardown instead of explicit cleanup on timeout/failure
findings.claim: The test's poll loop has a 5s deadline, but on timeout unwrap() panics before use_keyspace_sender is dropped and before worker.await runs, so cleanup relies on runtime teardown rather than explicit cleanup. In the keyspace test, proxy.finish() is likewise skipped when an assertion fails.

findings.title: Pre-existing wrong-shard drop path still omits dec_total_connections
findings.claim: The wrong-shard drop path still drops a counted connection without calling dec_total_connections, a gap predating this PR. The metrics-balancing commit de164845 doesn't fix this path, so the total-connections metric can still drift.

findings.title: decrement_total_connections could batch per-connection fetch_sub calls into one
findings.claim: decrement_total_connections runs one atomic fetch_sub(1) per connection instead of a single batched update; a dec_total_connections_by(n) helper would reduce it to one update. The report explicitly frames this as a simplification suggestion, not a defect.

findings.title: Commit message omits most of what the commit actually changes
findings.claim: Commit 7f48315d's subject 'discard connections after keyspace setup failure' omits the new public ConnectionError::UseKeyspaceError variant and its From impl, the warn! to debug! log-level change, and the reordering of keyspace setup ahead of maybe_reshard and the shard-aware port update. None of the four commits has a body, so the checklist item asserting commit messages explain what changes and why is false.

findings.title: Metric fix is split from its tests, plus an unnecessary fixup commit
findings.claim: The metric fix de164845 ships with no tests; its tests only arrive in the later commit 0d91aa54, and commit 617139df merely tweaks a wait in a test that 0d91aa54 added, so it should be squashed rather than left as a separate fixup commit.

findings.title: PR issue reference 'Fixes: #1682' is broken (404)
findings.claim: The PR's 'Fixes: #1682' reference returns 404 in dkropachev/quillstone, i.e. it points to a nonexistent issue.

findings.title: No Claude/Anthropic attribution found in PR or commits
findings.claim: The report checked for Claude/Anthropic attribution in the PR and commits and found none present.

findings.title: New error message wording is inconsistent with existing UseKeyspaceError variants
findings.claim: The new UseKeyspaceError variant's message doesn't match the pattern of neighboring setup variants, which use #[error(transparent)], nor the three existing UseKeyspaceError wrappers that all say "'USE KEYSPACE <>' request failed: {0}"; the new variant introduces a fourth wording.

findings.title: New tests omit setup_tracing() that nearby tests consistently call
findings.claim: The new tests at connection_pool.rs:1474 and :1526 skip calling setup_tracing(), even though every nearby test, at lines 1728, 1781, 1869, 1945, 1973, 2047, and 2082, calls it.

findings.title: New tests duplicate existing test helpers instead of reusing them
findings.claim: The new tests build PoolRefiller by hand instead of using the existing mock_pool_refiller() helper, make_rules repeats the rules already in start_simulated_node, and unrequested_connection_event is nearly identical to shard_aware_attempt_result, differing only in requested_shard, with names that don't convey the similarity.

findings.title: Polling sleep in test makes it timing-dependent instead of deterministic
findings.claim: The test's 1ms poll on get_total_connections() is bounded by a timeout but still depends on timing; awaiting the refiller's pool_updated Notify, or driving handle_ready_connection directly, would make it deterministic instead.

findings.title: Metric decrement logic is duplicated across multiple clear sites
findings.claim: The metric decrement is repeated at each clear site, lines 674-677, 1031-1032, 1114-1117, 1360, so any future site that clears conns or excess_connections must remember to also decrement, and the per-connection loop at 1361 repeats the same metric call. The two failure arms at 890-911 repeat the same bookkeeping and could drift apart over time.

findings.title: PR description claims refill recovery without noting it can never succeed
findings.claim: The PR description says the pool 'schedules another refill' but doesn't disclose that for a persistent keyspace error the refill repeats the same failing prerequisite and can never succeed. It frames this as recovery, but the pool instead ends up Broken, whereas base kept serving.

findings.title: Keyspace setup now gates sharding updates, with undocumented staleness window
findings.claim: In base, maybe_reshard, the shard-aware port update, and the advanced shard-awareness check ran before the keyspace step; now they only run after USE succeeds, and this ordering change is undocumented. While failures continue, sharder, shard_aware_port, and the shard-awareness block stay stale, so refills open shard-aware connections with the old sharder or port. The test asserts refiller.sharder.is_none() after a failure and the PR body mentions completing keyspace setup before resharding, but doesn't describe the stale period or that a USE with no timeout also holds back sharding updates.

findings.title: PR body omits most of the actual change (metric commits, new error variant, log change)
findings.claim: The PR body leaves out the metric-balancing commits de164845, 0d91aa54, and 617139df, their three tests, the new public ConnectionError::UseKeyspaceError variant, and the log-level change. The validation section lists only the two keyspace_setup_failure tests, which do exist, but doesn't show whether the metrics feature was enabled for them.
